### gnome-extensions info fuckwayland-bridge@fuckwayland
fuckwayland-bridge@fuckwayland
  Name: fuckwayland bridge
  Description: Exports Mutter window, workspace and monitor control over D-Bus (org.fuckwayland.Bridge) so wdotool, wwmctl and wxprop can drive a GNOME Wayland session. wxrandr and warandr do not need it: monitors go through Mutter's own DisplayConfig.
  Path: /usr/share/gnome-shell/extensions/fuckwayland-bridge@fuckwayland
  URL: https://github.com/antoniobianchi333/fuckwayland
  Version: 3
  Enabled: Yes
  State: ACTIVE
### rc=0
### gnome-extensions info fuckwayland-overlap@fuckwayland
fuckwayland-overlap@fuckwayland
  Name: fuckwayland overlap (unsupported)
  Description: Lets wxrandr --unsafe-gnome-overlap place two GNOME monitors so that they share screen area, which Mutter's own configuration API refuses. It does nothing at all until it is called, and it re-checks this build of libmutter before every write. Only GNOME Shell 46, 50 and 51 have been measured; on anything else it refuses. Not needed by any other fuckwayland tool.
  Path: /usr/share/gnome-shell/extensions/fuckwayland-overlap@fuckwayland
  URL: https://github.com/antoniobianchi333/fuckwayland
  Version: 1
  Enabled: Yes
  State: ACTIVE

### rc=0
### wxrandr --dryrun --unsafe-gnome-overlap --output Virtual-2 --pos 1000x0
xrandr: --unsafe-gnome-overlap: GNOME will not place these monitors, so they are going to be
  placed by writing into the running gnome-shell instead of asking it.
  What it does:         move Virtual-2 from +1920+0 to +1000+0
                        by writing 8 bytes per monitor inside gnome-shell
                        (GNOME Shell 46.0), through the fuckwayland-overlap@fuckwayland
                        extension, and then asking Mutter to apply the result.
  What it risks:        those 8 bytes go where this build of libmutter keeps a
                        logical monitor's position.  The extension re-checks
                        that this really is such a build before every write --
                        struct size against the GType registry, a sentinel
                        through Mutter's own setter, and every value it reads
                        against what Mutter reports publicly -- and refuses if
                        anything disagrees.  If all of that is wrong anyway,
                        gnome-shell crashes, and on Wayland gnome-shell is the
                        session: every program running in it goes with it.
  What it saves:        nothing.  ~/.config/monitors.xml is never written on
                        this path, so this layout does not survive a logout,
                        and --persistent is refused together with this flag.
  To undo:              wxrandr --output Virtual-1 --pos 0x0 --output Virtual-2 --pos 1920x0 --output Virtual-3 --pos 3840x0
                        or log out and back in.
  If the session dies:  gnome-shell is the session on Wayland, so you land at
                        the login screen.  Log in again -- nothing was saved,
                        so the layout is the one you started with.
                        If a session will not start at all, switch to a text
                        console with Ctrl+Alt+F3, log in and run
                            gnome-extensions disable fuckwayland-overlap@fuckwayland
                        (or delete whichever of these two is there:
                            ~/.local/share/gnome-shell/extensions/fuckwayland-overlap@fuckwayland
                            /usr/share/gnome-shell/extensions/fuckwayland-overlap@fuckwayland   <- from the .deb ),
                        then Ctrl+Alt+F1 back to the login screen.
xrandr: GNOME's rule this breaks: logical monitors not adjacent (an overlap counts, and so does a gap)
xrandr: overlap check shell-version: GNOME Shell 46.0, libmutter-14.so.0 (build 9e23feb34618)
xrandr: overlap check typelib: FwOverlap14, MetaMonitorsConfig 72 bytes as declared
xrandr: overlap check sentinel: switch_config round-tripped at the declared offset
xrandr: overlap check pending-dialog: nothing holds a modal grab, so GNOME is not asking "Keep changes?"
xrandr: overlap check bounded-read: 3 logical monitors, every address range-checked
xrandr: overlap check public-view: identical to Mutter's public view (global.display + get_monitor_for_connector on the requested names)
xrandr: dryrun: nothing was written
screen 0: 5760x1080 1520x285 mm  96.25dpi
crtc 1:    1920x1080  75.00 +1000+0 "Virtual-2"
